page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25% tier. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. The processor supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, which assist in vector calculations and cryptography tasks. Text processing benchmarks also show strong performance, while database operations, static web serving, and Redis SET operations perform at average levels.

The instance offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require high memory density, as the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio prioritizes processing power over memory capacity. The lack of local storage requires users to provision external network storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs. This configuration is suitable for compute-bound tasks, web serving, software compilation, and lightweight cryptography workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor at 2.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and KVM hypervisor, this instance provides a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, making it highly efficient for processing-intensive tasks. Benchmark data shows strong single-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench tests, alongside average multi-core and database execution speeds. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. It supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI. This hardware profile is well-suited for compute-bound applications, software compilation, text processing, and web serving workloads where high memory density is not required.
